questions.stem_text:
When a claim is supported only by asserting that unidentified experts accept the claim the
arguer has committed which of the following fallacies?
questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: D - appeal to anonymous authority

questions.stem_text: On McGregor's view, our rights carve out

options.A: the boundaries of our moral obligations.
options.B: the domain of our personal identity.
options.D: what we are free to do.
options.E: the responsibilities we have towards others.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: B - the domain of our personal identity.

questions.stem_text:
When Euthyphro attempts to define the holy as prosecuting wrongdoers, Socrates objects
that:

options.A: it is impossible for humans to judge what is holy.
options.B: there are many other things that are also holy.
options.C: the concept of 'wrongdoing' is too subjective to define holiness.
options.D: only gods can decide who the wrongdoers are.
options.E: Euthyphro is not a reliable authority on what is holy.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: B - there are many other things that are also holy.

questions.stem_text: One suggestion that Lukianoff and Haidt make to challenge vindictive protectiveness is

options.A: to implement stricter guidelines for classroom discussions.
options.B: to promote greater understanding of historical and contemporary oppression.
options.C: to increase the number of safe spaces on campus.
options.D: to mandate sensitivity training for all students.
options.E: to increase funding for mental health services on campus.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - to implement stricter guidelines for classroom discussions.
